tasks.short: Summarize continuity exercises, assess recovery gaps, and recommend corrective actions.

steps.what: Collect the exercise objectives, scenario, schedule, and approved recovery procedures.
Export recorded exercise events, recovery timings, and unresolved incidents.
Debrief participants about decisions, workarounds, failures, and missing observations.
Reconcile event timings and calculate recovery performance against agreed targets.
Assess failure causes, evidence limits, business consequences, and corrective priorities.
Write the exercise report, covering preparation, execution, findings, conclusions, and recommendations.

loop.input: Report template, exercise references, calculated results, and the planner's assessed findings.
loop.output: Draft exercise report with source references and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections, source identifiers, and numerical consistency; planner reviews narrative accuracy.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per report; unresolved claims return to manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle tables and headings; varied observations require concise narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Approve the report and agree corrective owners, priorities, and deadlines.
Publish the approved report with its supporting evidence and access restrictions.
Record the approved corrective actions in the delivery tracker.

tasks.design: Configured exports from {HELPDESK} and references from {DOCS} feed deterministic recovery calculations on {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded drafting loop fills the report template using the planner's findings and traceable evidence. After the risk owner approves publication and corrective actions, {WORKFLOW} publishes to {DOCS} and creates actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence had inconsistent timestamps and separate document versions. Narrative assembly still required substantial manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, reusable templates, and faster code development make evidence assembly affordable. Bounded drafting can summarize supplied observations.
tasks.still_hard: Exercise logs rarely explain why people improvised. Conflicting accounts and unrealistic test conditions still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an apparently successful recovery concealed unsafe workarounds or depended on one unusually capable person.
tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time assembling reports and more time comparing recurring weaknesses. The risk owner can delegate corrective-action prioritization within an agreed remediation budget.

reach.task: Turn approved recovery fixes into deliverable remediation work.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, acceptance criteria, and verification of action closure.

evidence.claim: Structured timestamps and recovery targets support deterministic calculations; causal conclusions need human assessment.
Source-constrained drafting is feasible, but the digest provides no continuity-report implementation case.
A documented report with nonexistent sources led to a partial refund, supporting explicit source validation.

assumptions: This describes a mid-size European company using document plans and a ticket-based exercise log.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.
The first build covers one exercise format and excludes automatic causal conclusions.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Whether exercise events are recorded in {HELPDESK}, documents, or another available slot.
Whether timestamps, recovery targets, and source versions are reliable.
Who can approve corrective spending and report distribution.
Whether observations contain personal data requiring additional access restrictions.
research_questions: Can the calculation reproduce the last exercise report and expose its missing evidence?
Does factual review take less time than drafting from scratch?
new_work: Review narrative claims and unresolved timing exceptions.
Maintain report templates, target definitions, and source mappings.
Check that approved actions retain their owners and evidence links.

tasks.short: Create and deliver continuity training, awareness materials, and follow-up learning.

steps.what: Agree audiences, learning goals, delivery format, and practical disruption scenarios.
Find current procedures, contact routes, and approved messages for the training.
Prepare slides, facilitator notes, quick guides, and practice questions.

loop.input: Approved procedures, audience brief, training templates, and permitted practice scenarios.
loop.output: Draft training pack with procedure references and answer keys.
loop.check: Verify references and required sections; flag unsupported instructions and check answers against approved procedures.
loop.stop: One generation and one revision per pack; unresolved instructions require manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble material; adapting explanations and practice questions to different roles requires language generation.

steps.what: Check operational accuracy, accessibility, and safety instructions before approving release.
Publish approved learning materials and enrol the agreed audiences.
Book sessions and send joining details to participants.
Deliver training, facilitate practice, and discuss participants' concerns and questions.
Record attendance, check completion, and assign agreed follow-up learning.

tasks.design: A template generator uses versioned procedures in {DOCS} and a bounded loop to draft role-specific materials. The safety lead approves instructions before configured flows publish to {LMS} and schedule sessions in {CALENDAR}. Human facilitation continues, while {LMS} handles completion records and agreed reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tailoring materials for different roles was labour intensive. Training administration and procedure updates were handled separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable layouts, source references, and bounded drafting reduce preparation time. Existing learning and calendar functions can handle administration.
tasks.still_hard: People need practice under realistic constraints. Language, accessibility, shift patterns, and local safety arrangements require deliberate adaptation.
tasks.human_edge: Build confidence, notice misunderstandings, and create enough trust for staff to disclose impractical procedures.
tasks.altitude: The planner can spend more time facilitating practice and resolving questions. With delegated authority, they can choose audience-specific examples and delivery formats within approved safety instructions.

reach.task: Organize continuity induction for temporary staff and workplace support teams.
reach.learn: Audience access, shift coverage, accessible communication, and induction logistics.

evidence.claim: Template-based materials and bounded source-based drafting can reduce preparation work; human facilitation remains valuable.
Learning systems commonly support enrolment, completion records, and reminders.
GDPR applies to identifiable attendance records; consultation and employment requirements depend on national rules.

assumptions: The company combines live continuity sessions with materials held in {DOCS} and completion tracking in {LMS}.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one training programme.
Follow-up rules concern learning administration and do not make employment decisions.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Whether temporary staff currently receive continuity induction.
Which languages, accessibility formats, and shift arrangements are needed.
Who approves safety instructions and training audiences.
Whether completion records influence employment decisions.
research_questions: Can participants explain the correct first actions after using the generated materials?
Which questions reveal a faulty procedure rather than a training gap?
new_work: Review generated instructions, examples, and answer keys.
Refresh training when approved procedures change.
Handle enrolment exceptions and inaccessible learning formats.
Turn unresolved learner questions into procedure corrections.

tasks.short: Design and implement practical tools and services that reduce disruption risk.

steps.what: Collect recovery gaps, current procedures, and requests for improved continuity tools.
Agree operational needs, fallback arrangements, users, and acceptable recovery outcomes.
Compare approved solution patterns, costs, dependencies, and expected recovery coverage.
Select a solution and approve its scope, costs, limitations, and acceptance criteria.
Configure a prototype with forms, fallback checklists, escalation rules, and status records.
Test normal operation, lost connectivity, failed dependencies, and recovery acceptance criteria.
Authorize deployment after reviewing test evidence, residual risk, and rollback arrangements.
Deploy the approved configuration and verify access, ownership, and fallback availability.

tasks.design: A solution catalogue in {DOCS} and deterministic comparison on {DATA_PLATFORM} turn agreed requirements into transparent options. Approved templates in {WORKFLOW} provide continuity forms, checklists, escalation flows, and status records. Repeatable tests produce acceptance evidence before a risk owner authorizes deployment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each tool request became a small bespoke project. Requirements, dependencies, and acceptance tests were rarely reusable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing workflow components and faster implementation of comparison and test utilities lower the cost of small tools. No model loop is needed for the scoped solution.
tasks.still_hard: A tool may fail during the same disruption it is meant to manage. Independent access, realistic recovery tests, and unsupported requirements remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choose workable compromises between recovery speed, safety, cost, and the burden placed on operational teams.

ambition.what: Continuity tool clinic for small operational teams

tasks.altitude: The planner spends more time shaping requirements and testing whether tools work under disruption. Delegated authority can let them approve small configurations within a defined budget and risk envelope.

reach.task: Specify and test continuity workflows and their failure modes.
reach.learn: Access design, dependency isolation, acceptance testing, and rollback planning.

reach.task: Validate fallback access when a workplace or building service is unavailable.
reach.learn: Physical access dependencies and practical workplace recovery constraints.

evidence.claim: Forms, records, rule-based escalation, and comparisons can be built from configured components and deterministic code.
Recovery tools require testing against shared dependencies and loss of their usual access path.
The digest contains no direct implementation case for continuity-tool design or its expected savings.

assumptions: The typical case is a small internal workflow or records tool, not replacement of critical infrastructure.
An existing {WORKFLOW} supports the necessary configuration and access controls.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one limited tool.
Human tests remain necessary for physical and organisational failure scenarios.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which existing configuration capabilities and reusable components are available.
Whether recovery access depends on the same infrastructure as normal operations.
Which integrations can operate during an outage.
Who can accept residual risk and authorize deployment.
Whether the tool processes employee data or changes working arrangements.
research_questions: Which requests can be satisfied by existing configuration without a new application?
Can users complete the recovery workflow when normal identity, network, or workplace access fails?
new_work: Maintain approved solution patterns and realistic cost assumptions.
Test configuration changes and shared dependency failures.
Handle requirements that exceed existing component capabilities.
Keep deployment, rollback, and fallback instructions current.

tasks.short: Define and implement monitoring and response methods for safety, operational, and compliance interruptions.

steps.what: Review interruption records, recurring failures, response delays, and unresolved actions.
Identify monitoring and response requirements in approved procedures and compliance guidance.

loop.input: Approved procedures and compliance guidance with versioned source identifiers.
loop.output: Candidate requirements, response owners, timing conditions, and source passages.
loop.check: Verify each source passage and retain qualifiers; planner checks completeness and interpretation.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; ambiguous requirements go to the responsible specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements and exceptions appear in varied prose; keyword rules cannot reliably preserve their conditions.

steps.what: Agree detectable warning signs, response ownership, escalation paths, and operational constraints.
Specify indicators, thresholds, escalation timings, and checks for missing or stale signals.
Approve monitoring thresholds, escalation rules, and permitted automatic actions.
Configure monitoring feeds, notification rules, routing, and response timers.
Evaluate flagged interruptions, missed signals, false alarms, and response performance.
Agree and authorize corrective responses, assigning accountable operational owners.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop turns approved guidance in {DOCS} into candidate requirements for human review. Configured {WORKFLOW} rules connect permitted signals from {OPS_SYSTEM} and records from {HELPDESK}, checking thresholds and signal freshness. Views in {HELPDESK} show exceptions and response ownership; operational interventions require the incident coordinator's authorization.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were buried in prose, and signals had inconsistent ownership. Connecting monitoring, escalation, and response records required bespoke coordination.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing routing and reporting functions cover much of the work. Faster integration development and bounded extraction make a limited monitoring service affordable.
tasks.still_hard: A silent signal can mean normal operation or failed monitoring. Alert fatigue, incomplete coverage, and safety consequences require realistic tests and operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret an interruption in context and coordinate a response when safety, service, and compliance priorities conflict.

ambition.what: Weekly review of interruption thresholds and missed warnings

tasks.altitude: The planner spends less time collecting incident summaries and more time testing whether warnings lead to useful responses. Delegated authority can allow low-risk routing adjustments within approved limits; operational intervention rights remain with the incident coordinator.

reach.task: Evaluate whether interruption controls detect failures and produce effective corrective action.
reach.learn: Control effectiveness, missed-event analysis, false-alarm measurement, and corrective-action verification.

reach.task: Connect workplace service interruptions to continuity escalation.
reach.learn: Building-service signals, local response authority, and fallback communication.

evidence.claim: Threshold checks, signal-freshness checks, routing, and response timers can use deterministic rules.
Extracting requirements from varied prose benefits from bounded language processing and specialist review.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply according to the actual processing and AI use; national consultation rules vary.

assumptions: The typical implementation supports detection and coordination rather than controlling safety equipment.
Automatic actions are limited to approved internal notifications, ticket routing, and timers.
Time shares, remaining time, and build ranges are estimates for one service or site.
The scoped monitoring uses service signals rather than individual employee surveillance.
The access range includes employee consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Which warning signals exist, how fresh they are, and who maintains them.
Whether the available feeds remain accessible during disruption.
Which national rules and sector-specific obligations apply.
Whether monitoring includes identifiable employee activity.
Who can approve thresholds and authorize operational interventions.
research_questions: Do historical interruptions show warnings that the proposed rules would have detected?
Can missing or stale signals be distinguished from healthy service status?
Do test alerts reach an available owner through a functioning fallback channel?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve ambiguous obligations.
Investigate false alarms, missed interruptions, and stale feeds.
Maintain signal mappings, response rosters, and escalation rules.
Retest approved controls after service or procedure changes.

role.altitude: The continuity planner's week shifts toward recovery trade-offs, realistic exercises, facilitation, and control effectiveness. Delegated rights can cover small tool configurations, training formats, and low-risk routing changes within approved limits; risk acceptance and operational intervention stay with their accountable owners.
reach: Project management specialists: translate recovery gaps into verifiable remediation work.
Computer systems analysts: configure and test continuity tools against dependency failures.
Facilities managers: connect physical workplace constraints with recovery and escalation arrangements.
Quality control systems managers: test whether continuity controls detect failures and drive effective correction.
skills_to_grow: Structured recovery evidence and dependency mapping.
Configuration of forms, records, reports, and escalation rules.
Source checking and review of bounded model outputs.
Failure testing, fallback access, and rollback planning.
GDPR handling, AI-use assessment, and consultation under applicable national rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a small-team continuity service combining practical tool clinics, temporary-staff induction, and recurring failure reviews. Give teams tested recovery tools and clear escalation routes, with measured evidence of where recovery still depends on fragile assumptions.
